The high uncertainty in bloc arithmetic and coalition formation dynamics supports a moderate-to-high probability for Netanyahu not returning as PM, but not an overwhelming one given how often such predictions have been wrong for him historically.

xvenue.read: polyMoves = minutes where Polymarket's mid moved >= 3c; staleKalshi = of those, Kalshi's same-minute quote was still crossable after its 7.000000000000001% x p(1-p) taker fee (avgStaleEdgeC = cents of edge per share); kalshiSameMin/NextMin = Kalshi moved the same way that minute / the next; kalshiLeads = Kalshi moved first and Polymarket followed. A Kalshi lane is worth building only if staleRate x avgStaleEdgeC is meaningfully positive over many games. us* = the same for Polymarket US (taker 6.950000000000001% x p(1-p)); kUsCross = minutes where buying on one US-legal venue and selling on the other cleared both taker fees (the only fully legal arbitrage pair for a US operator).

usLane.read: Paper only: each event is a hypothetical taker fill on Polymarket US at the sampled quote (px, qty = shares shown at that price; one event per game minute, on the leg the US instrument quotes). tradable = the subset with at least 50 shares shown (usd = dollars on the shown size, capped at 1000 shares) in a minute where global Polymarket's mid moved >= 3c and the US quote was still crossable after the 6.950000000000001% x p(1-p) taker fee (edgeC = cents of edge at entry). marks.* = cents per share after the entry fee, marked at global Polymarket's mid 1/5/15/60 minutes later and at the end of the game (final), and at settlement (0/1). Exit fees and the US spread are not charged. roiPct = avg mark pnl / avg entry price. noData = horizon passed with no sample. Decision rule (docs/PROFIT-AVENUES.md Part 2): after ~200 events, if m15 and settle are both positive after fees with a hit rate above 50% and the shown size is tradable, a Polymarket US lane is worth building; the real-money flip stays the operator's call.
